title: Signed box document
description: The envelope wrapping every signed document. The payload travels as exact base64-encoded JSON so that verifying a signature means hashing the bytes as transmitted, with no canonical-JSON implementation to keep in sync across languages. Passing this schema means the envelope is well-formed, never that its signature is valid.

payloadBase64.description: The document payload: UTF-8 JSON, base64-encoded, signed and hashed exactly as it appears here.

payloadSha256.description: SHA-256 of the decoded payload bytes.

signatures.description: Detached signatures over the decoded payload bytes. A verifier accepts the document when any one signature verifies against a trusted key, which is what allows a key to be rotated without reissuing every document.
